## 型

### TaskGroup

```emela
effect TaskGroup[E, R]
```

The capability to start tasks whose results are awaited. `E` and `R` are the `fails` and
`uses` of the tasks. Only `Task.Group` provides it (`[task.group]`).

- `fn start[A](f: fn() -> A fails E uses { TaskGroup[E, R], R }) -> Task[A]`

  Starts `f` as a task of the group. The task starts running the next time the starting task
  suspends. `f` may use the group itself, to start siblings.

### Task

```emela
type Task[A]
```

A task started in a group. It lives only while the capability of the group does
(`[task.group]`).

### Group

```emela
handler Group[E, R]: TaskGroup[E, R]
```

Provides TaskGroup. When the body ends, its release interrupts the tasks left and waits until
they have unwound. A failure of a task interrupts its siblings and fails the with.

### Spawn

```emela
effect Spawn[E, R]
```

The capability to start tasks whose results are not awaited. Only `Task.Background` provides it
(`[task.background]`).

- `fn start(f: fn() -> () fails E uses { Spawn[E, R], R }) -> ()`

  Starts `f` as a task. The task starts running the next time the starting task suspends.

### Background

```emela
handler Background[E, R]: Spawn[E, R]
init(on_failure: fn(Cause[E]) -> () uses { R })
```

Provides Spawn. Its release waits until the tasks have ended, without interrupting them. A
failure of a task goes to `on_failure`, called in that task after it has unwound.

## 値

### join

```emela
fn join[A](task: Task[A]) -> A uses { Async, task }
```

Waits for the task to end and returns its value.

### all

```emela
fn all[A, E, R](fs: List[fn() -> A fails E uses { R }]) -> List[A] fails E uses { Async, R }
```

Runs all of `fs` concurrently and returns their values in order. If one fails, the others are
interrupted and `all` fails.

### race

```emela
fn race[A, E, R](fs: List[fn() -> A fails E uses { R }]) -> A fails E uses { Async, R }
```

Runs all of `fs` concurrently and takes the first to end; the others are interrupted. If the
first to end fails, `race` fails with that error.

### both

```emela
fn both[A, B, E, R](f: fn() -> A fails E uses { R }, g: fn() -> B fails E uses { R }) -> (A, B) fails E uses { Async, R }
```

Runs `f` and `g` concurrently and returns both values. If one fails, the other is interrupted
and `both` fails.

### map

```emela
fn map[A, B, E, R](xs: List[A], f: fn(A) -> B fails E uses { R }) -> List[B] fails E uses { Async, R }
```

Applies `f` to each element of `xs` concurrently and returns the results in order. If one
fails, the others are interrupted and `map` fails.

### timeout

```emela
fn timeout[A, E, R](ms: Int, f: fn() -> A fails E uses { R }) -> Option[A] fails E uses { Async, Clock, R }
```

Waits for `f` up to `ms` milliseconds. Returns `Some` with its value if it ends in time;
otherwise interrupts it and returns `None`. Wrap it in `Option.or_fail` to fail instead. The
time is measured with `Clock`.
